extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors reporting in vivo animal studies (preclinical biomedical researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how to report the conduct, welfare, husbandry, ethical approval, monitoring, interpretation, limitations and generalisability of animal experiments so that studies are transparent, reproducible and ethically justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the name of the ethical review committee or equivalent that has approved the use of animals in this study and any relevant licence or protocol numbers (if applicable). If ethical approval was not sought or granted, provide a justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must comply with regulations/guidelines and ensure relevant approval from an appropriate ethics committee/regulatory body before work starts. Provide a clear statement explaining how the study conforms to appropriate regulations and guidelines, include the institution and committee (e.g. IACUC, AWERB) and indicate protocol or project licence numbers and any relevant accreditation (e.g. AAALAC, GLP). If formal approval is not required, demonstrate compliance with international standards and explain why the research is exempt. Examples show full citation of Acts, named review boards and licence numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and husbandry
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of housing and husbandry conditions, including any environmental enrichment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report environmental factors that determine animal health/wellbeing and can affect behavioural and physiological responses (and thus study outcomes). Consider reporting cage/tank/housing system (type, dimensions), food and water (type, composition, supplier, access), bedding and nesting material, temperature and humidity, sanitation (frequency, water quality), social environment (group size/composition/stocking density), biosecurity status, lighting (type/schedule/intensity), and environmental enrichment (structural enrichment, species-typical resources, toys, exercise). If no enrichment provided, state with justification. Provide scientific justification for withholding food/water or for single housing. If space is limited, provide these details via a public repository or supplementary information. Examples illustrate complete reporting (IVC details, temperature, humidity, caging density, diet, enrichment, accreditation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring — pain/suffering reduction (16a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any interventions or steps taken in the experimental protocols to reduce pain, suffering, and distress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a thorough description of pain management strategies including the specific analgesic, administration method (formulation, route, dose, concentration, volume, frequency, timing, equipment), rationale for choice (model, disease, procedure, mechanism, pharmacokinetics, personnel safety), protocol modifications to reduce pain (changes to anaesthesia, increased monitoring, habituation), and any other welfare measures. If analgesics or welfare measures expected for the procedure were omitted for experimental reasons, report the scientific justification. Examples include dosing regimens, voluntary ingestion methods, and escalation plans tied to pain scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring — adverse events reporting (16b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report any expected or unexpected adverse events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report adverse events that negatively impacted welfare (cardiovascular/respiratory depression, CNS disturbance, hypothermia, reduced food intake, etc.), indicate whether they were expected or unexpected. If no adverse events were observed or recorded, explicitly state this. Reporting adverse events helps others plan welfare assessments and assess risk–benefit for interventions; examples demonstrate detailed logging and consequences (e.g. humane killing and autopsy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring — humane endpoints and monitoring (16c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the humane endpoints established for the study, the signs that were monitored, and the frequency of monitoring. If the study did not have humane endpoints, state this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define predetermined morphological, physiological and/or behavioural signs that trigger removal from the study. Report endpoints established for the specific species/strain, clear criteria of clinical signs monitored and those that led to euthanasia or other actions (general welfare indicators and procedure-specific indicators like tumour size or sensory-motor deficits). Report timing and frequency of monitoring, taking circadian rhythms and critical post-procedural times into account. Publishing clinical sign score sheets is encouraged. Always state if no humane endpoints were established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation / scientific implications (17a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret the results, taking into account the study objectives and hypotheses, current theory, and other relevant studies in the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret results in context of study objectives; for hypothesis-testing studies, restrict interpretations to the primary outcome (exploratory outcomes should not be presented as conclusive). Discuss findings in relation to current theory and ideally systematic reviews; avoid selectively citing only supportive or statistically significant studies. Where appropriate, describe implications for improving welfare or reducing animal numbers (e.g. methods that reduce variability and allow smaller group sizes). Examples show contrasting with prior data and potential to reduce animal use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on study limitations (17b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on the study limitations including potential sources of bias, limitations of the animal model, and imprecision associated with the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss unavoidable limitations to place findings in context and to guide future experiments. Consider the quality of evidence and appropriateness of the animal model. Discuss internal validity and whether risks of bias were addressed by sample size, inclusion/exclusion criteria, randomisation and blinding. Explicitly acknowledge limitations and their implications for interpretation and generalisability; examples include unmeasured infection sources, model-specific mechanistic limits, and extrapolation caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability / translation (18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on whether, and how, the findings of this study are likely to generalise to other species or experimental conditions, including any relevance to human biology (where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess implications for further in vivo research or other domains (e.g. human trials). Discuss whether evidence is sufficient for translation or further study, and outline additional research needed. Consider factors that might moderate effects (population age/sex/strain/species, intervention differences, outcome measures). Interpret results in relation to existing evidence (similar or supporting findings). Thoughtful consideration can reduce unnecessary or wasteful follow-up studies and inform translational decisions.
